meta.title: FAQ - Frequently asked questions
meta.description: Answers to common questions about Argos: how it works, reports, analysis limits, privacy and what's coming next.

hero.title: Frequently asked questions
hero.sub: Everything you need to know about Argos, reports, analysis limits and how your data is handled.

items.a: Argos is a website audit tool: you submit a URL, five analysis modules run in sequence (HTTP, HTML, performance, Lighthouse, security) and you get a scored, prioritized report with concrete actions to take.
Yes. Analysis is completely free, with no account to create and no credit card required.

items.q: How long does an analysis take?
items.a: A full analysis takes about 20 to 30 seconds. The report page updates automatically once the audit is complete.
Any public site reachable over HTTP or HTTPS. For security reasons, local or private addresses (localhost, internal networks) are blocked.
An overall score, detailed scores per category (performance, security, SEO, accessibility) and a list of prioritized issues, sorted by severity, with recommended actions.
No. Each report is accessible through a URL containing a unique token. It is not indexed by search engines and stays private unless you share the link.
Yes. Just send the report link: anyone with the link can view it. Only share it with people you trust.

items.q: How long does a report stay available?
items.a: Reports have an expiration date. After that, the link is no longer valid and you need to run a new analysis to get an up-to-date report.

Five modules: HTTP headers, HTML structure and SEO, runtime metrics (perceived performance), Lighthouse scores (performance, accessibility, best practices, SEO) and security (SSL, security headers, basic vulnerability scan).

items.q: Does Argos replace a manual audit?
items.a: No. Argos gives a fast, prioritized automated diagnosis. It does not replace the expertise of an in-depth audit performed by a specialist.
Most often because the site is unreachable, too slow to respond, or blocks bots. Check that the URL is correct and publicly accessible, then try again.

items.q: Is there a limit on the number of analyses?
items.a: There is no strict quota for normal use. Reasonable usage is expected to keep the service fast and reliable for everyone.
Argos keeps the analyzed URL and the generated report for as long as needed to display it. No personal data is required to run an analysis.
Only people who have the link containing the report token. Reports are neither listed publicly nor indexed.

items.q: Do my reports show up in Google?
items.a: No. Report pages are marked as non-indexable and protected by a token, so they don't appear in search results.
Basic analysis is meant to stay free. Advanced features may be offered later as part of a dedicated plan.
Ideas under consideration include tracking score changes over time, comparing analyses, exporting reports and API access. Nothing is set in stone yet.

items.q: How can I stay informed about new features?
items.a: You can subscribe to the newsletter from the home page to be notified about updates and new features.

measurementCoverage.title: Measurement coverage
measurementCoverage.explanation: Weighted share of the scoring catalogue actually measured. Below 80% overall or in an applicable domain, the score remains provisional and must not be compared with a complete audit.
measurementCoverage.confidenceExplanation: Unavailable or blocked measurements are not site defects. Finding confidence remains separate from score coverage.

accessibility.title: Site accessibility
accessibility.intro: Test results and regulatory scope are two separate parts of this report.
accessibility.testsDescription: Automated checks identify some issues on the page analysed. Argos weights its checks; Lighthouse shows its raw score. The two scores can therefore differ.
accessibility.scopeSectionTitle: What is known about regulatory scope
accessibility.scopeDescription: This estimate depends on information about the service and its operator. It still needs human review.
accessibility.limit: These results are neither a complete RGAA/WCAG audit nor legal advice.

rulesReview.VALIDATED: Validation recorded for the rules used

accessibility.rulesSnapshot: This state and the rules version are preserved as of the report date. Validation does not certify the site’s compliance; later rule changes do not alter this report.

scopes.OUT_OF_SCOPE: Outside the reviewed scope after verification

riskReasons.RULES_PENDING: Qualification rules need human validation. No regulatory risk level is concluded.
riskReasons.SCOPE_UNKNOWN: The available information is insufficient to qualify the scope.
riskReasons.COLLECTION_INCOMPLETE: The collection is insufficient to establish a risk level.
riskReasons.FAILED_AUDITS: The indicative level uses failed automated audits and the reviewed scope, without a legal conclusion.
riskReasons.NO_DETECTED_FAILURE: No defect detected by the available checks does not prove conformance.
riskReasons.OUTSIDE_SCOPE: This determination only concerns the reviewed scope; it does not validate technical accessibility.

accessibility.elements: {count} elements reported in failed audits (not deduplicated across audits)
accessibility.truncated: The finding list is limited. The failed audit total includes audits that are not shown.
accessibility.noFailure: No defect detected in the available results. This does not mean the site conforms.
accessibility.qualificationTitle: View signals, missing information and sources
accessibility.noSignal: No sufficient signal observed; this does not prove exclusion.
accessibility.noMissing: No missing information recorded for the reviewed scope.
accessibility.manual: Keyboard navigation, focus, announcements and user journeys require human checks. Manual and not-applicable states are not passed tests.

IMAGE_ALTERNATIVE.title: Image text alternatives
IMAGE_ALTERNATIVE.impact: An image without an alternative may deny users its information.
IMAGE_ALTERNATIVE.recommendation: Check the purpose of each image; add a meaningful alternative or an empty one for decorative content.

CONTRAST.title: Text contrast
CONTRAST.impact: Insufficient contrast can make text difficult to read.
CONTRAST.recommendation: Check the colours in the affected states, improve contrast and verify manually.

ACCESSIBLE_NAME.title: Accessible control names
ACCESSIBLE_NAME.impact: A control without a meaningful name may be hard to understand with assistive technology.
ACCESSIBLE_NAME.recommendation: Associate an accessible label with the control and check its announcement in the user journey.

LANGUAGE.title: Page language
LANGUAGE.impact: A missing or incorrect language can affect screen reader pronunciation.
LANGUAGE.recommendation: Declare a valid language matching the content and check language changes.

OTHER.title: Lighthouse accessibility finding
OTHER.impact: An automated check reported a point to examine.
OTHER.recommendation: Inspect the identified Lighthouse audit and verify its impact on the user journey.

antiBot.title: Analysis may be partial
antiBot.description: This site is behind an anti-bot protection: the analysis ran against the challenge page and some results may be incomplete. This block is not counted against the score.

notFound.title: Report not found
notFound.description: This report doesn't exist, has expired, or the link is incorrect.

failed.title: The analysis failed
failed.description: Something went wrong while analyzing this site. Sorry for the inconvenience.

unavailable.rerunTitle: Run a new analysis, for free

hero.scoreTooltip: Aggregated score (0-100) based on detected issues.

oneLiner.high: Solid site: a few optimizations could further improve impact.
oneLiner.good: Good potential: targeted actions can improve performance and conversion.
oneLiner.fair: Several blockers: a small roadmap can quickly raise the score.
oneLiner.low: Big opportunities: fixing critical issues will improve trust and conversion.

footerCta.title: Schedule a call
footerCta.desc: 15 minutes to prioritize optimizations, estimate effort, and identify quick wins.

priorityCards.title: Recommended priorities
priorityCards.desc: Six distinct actions ranked by score contribution, then severity and available information.
priorityCards.modelLimit: Rubric estimate with constant measurements and denominators. Actual improvement depends on the fix and a new audit.

rankReasons.MODELLED_SCORE_GAIN: Ranked by avoidable score loss in its domain.
rankReasons.NO_DIRECT_SCORE_GAIN: Explanatory action without a direct score gain.
rankReasons.SCORE_UNAVAILABLE: Score contribution unavailable; ranked by severity.

priorityCards.effortTooltip: Indicative estimate (XS → L). Adjust based on project context.

categoryInfo.fallback: What this category measures and how it affects your site's quality.
categoryInfo.security: HTTP security: protection headers (HSTS, CSP…), information exposure and common vulnerabilities. A good score lowers attack risks (XSS, clickjacking).
categoryInfo.ssl: TLS/HTTPS certificate and encryption: supported protocol versions and configuration strength. Protects the confidentiality of exchanges.
categoryInfo.observatory: Mozilla Observatory analysis: recommended security headers and Content-Security-Policy. Reflects hardening best practices.
categoryInfo.seo: Search engine optimization: meta tags, heading structure and indexability. A good score improves visibility on search engines.
categoryInfo.a11y: Accessibility: how usable the site is for everyone, including assistive technologies (screen readers, keyboard navigation).
categoryInfo.performance: Loading speed and perceived smoothness (Core Web Vitals, resource weight). Directly impacts user experience and SEO.
categoryInfo.runtime: Behavior in a real browser: console errors, failed requests and rendering metrics (LCP, FCP). Surfaces issues visible to visitors.
categoryInfo.lighthouse: Google Lighthouse scores (performance, accessibility, best practices, SEO) measured on a real page load.

scoreGrid.title: Scores by category
scoreGrid.desc: Synthetic view for prioritization. Click a category to see details.
scoreGrid.globalTooltip: Aggregated global score (0-100) based on detected issues.
scoreGrid.partialTooltip: One or more modules could not be evaluated (service temporarily unavailable). The score covers the modules actually analyzed - the site is not penalized.

issuesByCategory.title: Details by category
issuesByCategory.desc: Filter by severity, then explore issues by category (sorted critical → info).

measures.title: Detectable accessibility

pme.exampleText: If a service page has a vague title, a heavy image, and no security policy, the report may surface those findings. Your team then decides what to change and checks the outcome.
limits: The audit covers the submitted URL, not every page on your site or your overall search ranking.
Argos does not observe your sales, form submissions, or conversion data.
Some checks may be unavailable when a page blocks bots; automated results do not replace a human audit.
pme.ctaText: Choose your home page or a service page, then use the findings as a starting point for a decision.

measures.title: Automated accessibility

benefits.title: Brief your team

limits: The audit checks only the submitted public page; it does not visit every product and category.

comparison.coverageChanged: Measurement coverage changed; this change is not a site regression.

reasons.NO_PREVIOUS_REPORT: No previous report in this history.
reasons.EVIDENCE_MISSING: Comparison unavailable: insufficient historical evidence. Run a new audit with the current policy.
reasons.METHODOLOGY_CHANGED: Comparison unavailable: different policy or coefficients.
reasons.INSUFFICIENT_COVERAGE: Comparison unavailable: insufficient coverage or anti-bot protection.

history.empty: No previous analysis for this URL.
